## Outcome and ownership
Child of #1357. Let a consumer declare the information required for a decision and receive either an authorized, evidence-complete bounded context or an explicit insufficient-context result.

Extend [pm-4k6b](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-4k6b.toon). Reuse complete reads and omission receipts (#947, #1035), exact delivery/source fingerprints (#1176), existing packing and [output sessions pm-hid9g1](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-hid9g1.toon). Existing byte/row completeness and token budgets are foundations; this slice adds task-semantic coverage across providers.

## Implementation plan
1. Define a versioned request contract: intent, scope/policy context, anchor IDs, mandatory/optional information categories, freshness bounds and token/latency limits. Categories are extensible; examples include active decision, blockers, latest verification, constraints and next safe action.
2. Establish an SDK provider interface declaring supported categories, source revisions, consistency/freshness guarantees and bounded reads. Scope and authorize before provider calls and before ranking.
3. Assemble from one coherent local revision or a validated revision vector. Read-start/read-end checks detect concurrent changes. For independent remote providers, expose the actual consistency class; refuse a strict snapshot request when a provider cannot prove it rather than implying cross-system atomicity.
4. Compute a coverage receipt with present, missing, stale, conflicted, unavailable, denied and budget-omitted states plus evidence references. Sensitive denied resources must not be enumerated to an unauthorized reader.
5. Preserve mandatory evidence while degrading optional detail. If mandatory evidence cannot fit or cannot be established, return a machine-readable insufficient-context outcome with safe next reads and minimum known additional requirements. Do not label partial context complete.
6. Key caches by source/dependency revisions, policy/visibility scope, intent, schema/provider version and projection/token profile. Expose a fingerprint and delta that identifies invalidated dependencies, including expiry and policy changes.
7. Make the public SDK the owner; wire CLI/MCP/package adapters and existing output-session deduplication to the same receipts. Measure the final emitted payload, including receipt overhead.

Illustrative names only: ContextRequirement, compileContext, ContextCoverageReceipt, ContextDependencyFingerprint.

## Acceptance and tests
- [ ] Required categories cannot disappear under top-k packing or a tiny token budget while the result remains sufficient
- [ ] Empty, missing, unavailable, expired, conflicting and truncated are distinguishable
- [ ] Two providers with divergent revisions cannot produce a falsely coherent result
- [ ] Changing a dependency, policy, provider schema or validity boundary invalidates cached coverage; unchanged dependencies support a stable compact delta
- [ ] High-ranking irrelevant content cannot displace mandatory decision evidence
- [ ] Provider timeout/failure and inaccessible sources yield bounded safe receipts without information leakage
- [ ] Tests cover concurrent mutation during assembly, strict versus best-effort consistency, tiny budgets, missing mandatory categories and changed decisions
- [ ] SDK/CLI/MCP fixtures agree on sufficiency and receipts; packed consumers and small/large workspaces pass existing latency/token gates

## Dependencies and non-goals
Integrate typed temporal knowledge and policy separation from #1357; scenario fixtures can precede implementation. No replacement ranker, second session ledger, mandatory distributed transaction coordinator, or guarantee that a provider supports a stronger snapshot than it declares.

## Linked implementation slices
- Depends on #1358 for temporal validity/conflict semantics and #1360 for scope/effect policy
- Supplies coverage fingerprints to #1359
- Verified by #1362
